newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European stocks slip after storming start.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European stocks slip after storming start.

text.p: European stock markets, fired up by Wall Street, rocketed ahead in early trade on Thursday but quickly fell back as an expected assault on the 5,000 point barrier in London failed to materialise.
On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar was firm and held on to its overnight gains above 116 yen after a smaller than expected rise in the Japanese trade surplus.
Before European markets opened, everyone forecast that Wall Street, where the Dow Jones Industrial Average broke through 8,000 points for the first time on Wednesday, would provoke another surge.
The Dow ended up 63.17 points at 8,038.88, little more than five months after it breached 7,000 on February 13.
But the predictions of a similar performance on leading European markets, which closed at record highs on Wednesday, proved only partially true.
In Paris, the CAC-40 index of blue chips stormed through 3,000 points at the opening for the first time.

"At the moment, everybody is looking through rose-tinted spectacles. The rise on Wall Street and the dollar is outweighing any fears one could have about the public deficit. We will see on Monday," said one trader.
But within 15 minutes the index had slipped back below 3,000 and by mid morning it was up a more modest 3.85 points at 2,991.86.

The deficit remained a nagging worry. Prime Minister Lionel Jospin is meeting ministers on Thursday to discuss budget measures which will be announced on Monday when an audit of the public finances is published.

Wall Street and the bullish dollar against the mark, also got the German market off to an enthusiastic start. "We are off like a rocket again," said a Frankfurt dealer in early trade. "There has to come a time when people ask themselves how long this frantic action can go on but it doesn't look like today's the day."

However, signs quickly emerged that sentiment might be changing more quickly than the dealer expected. The IBIS index of electronic trade was up 18.78 points at 4,242.47 at mid morning, but well below a 4,272.55 high reached earlier.
London also failed to live up to expectations. Before the opening dealers predicted that the FTSE-100 index of blue chips would break 5,000 points.

"I think everybody expected profit taking yesterday after the market was up three percent in five sessions," one dealer said. "When it didn't happen, those that were caught short had to come in and probably decided to buy even more."
But the FTSE stopped seven points of the 5,000 level before slipping. By mid morning it was down 0.1 at 4,964.1.
On the foreign exchanges, the dollar was firm above 116 yen and managed to nudge briefly above 1.80 marks amid market perceptions that the German government is tolerating the recent mark weakness.

"The view is both (the Bundesbank) and Bonn are not going to push for intervention or tightening monetary policy to adjust for market overreaction," said Sally Wilkinson, senior economist at Daiwa Europe. "I expect Bonn sees the overshoot as a relief for its export sector."

German Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Wednesday played down the recent mark weakness, saying short-term currency fluctuations were no grounds for worry. The government also issued a statement saying there was no reason to dramatise recent foreign exchange developments.
The dollar stood at 1.7963 marks, down from an early high of 1.8020 and just off late Wednesday's 1.7980.

Although the government statement gave ammunition to the dollar bulls, dealers said concern of intervention to brake the mark's weakness was still in traders' minds and likely to limit any aggressive dollar gains.
Intervention jitters were highlighted by unconfirmed talk that some European central banks were buying marks which was seen weighing on dollar/mark, said dealers.
The dollar also firmed above 116 yen overnight after news that the Japanese trade surplus rose over 934 billion yen year-on-year in June compared with a forecast rise of over one trillion yen.
However, analysts said the trend of a rising Japanese surplus would continue and was likely to keep dollar gains against the yen limited for some time.
The dollar was at 116.10 yen compared with 116.27 late on Wednesday in Europe.
CURRENCIES AT 0830 GMT
The dollar was at 116.10 yen and 1.7963 marks compared with 116.27 yen and 1.7980 marks in late trading on Wednessday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0900 gmt
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 0.1 at 4,964.1.
FRANKFURT - The IBIS index was up 18.78 points at 4,242.47.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 3.85 points at 2,991.86.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was at $318.95 an ounce compared with a Wednesday afternoon fixing of $319.50. Silver was at down 10 cents at $4.22.
